Basic dimensions printed: M17x1 d3 printed 15.733 (formula 15.773) and M48 D1 printed 42.857 (formula 42.587) look like transpositions; all other checked values agree with ISO 68-1 formulas to 0.001 mm. WIKI_UTS.title: Unified Thread Standard (main size table)

OPTIMAS_TOL.note: Header note 'Tolerances 6g (6h)'; M1 to M1.4 are printed with zero allowance (6h). M2.5 pitch max printed 2.118 (Ganter and the formula: 2.188).

GANTER_13.title: Metric ISO threads, tolerance fields 6g / 6H (DIN 13 extract, technical information 2393)
GANTER_13.note: Values with decimal commas. The M2.5 row could not be aligned reliably by the page reader; its external values 2.480/2.380/2.188/2.117 are recorded.

CDE_6H.title: Nuts: internal threads, class 6H, DIN 13; ISO 68 & ISO R 1501 (June 2000)

WIKI_IT.title: IT Grade (article, table of IT values)
WIKI_IT.note: IT01 to IT11 printed in um, IT12 to IT18 in mm (converted to um here, x1000).

GANTER_IT.title: DIN ISO 286 ISO-Grundtoleranzen, Auszug Teil 1 Zahlenwerte (technical appendix p. 2150)
GANTER_IT.note: Printed in um with decimal commas. IT18 over 315 to 400 printed as 2200, out of sequence with its neighbours (8100, 9700); recorded as printed.

GOST_25346.title: GOST 25346-89 Unified system of tolerances and fits, Tables 2 and 3 (national adoption of ISO 286-1:1988)
GOST_25346.note: Table 2 (shafts) and Table 3 (holes, page 65935_3/_4, including the delta values). Merged cells cover the main size step; recorded on the main step. f over 30 to 40 printed '25' without its sign in the transcription (column is negative); recorded as -25.

ROYMECH.title: ISO shaft fundamental deviations 0 to 500 mm
ROYMECH.note: The site does not permit substantial reproduction, so its table is not republished here. It was compared value by value with the GOST 25346 transcription for letters a to zc (except j, js, k): all 517 printed values are equal. Only its k column is recorded.

SIMPLYB.title: FAQ / ISO 286 Limits and Fits reference (shaft and hole limit deviations, ISO 286-2)
SIMPLYB.note: Prints limit deviations of tolerance classes for 3 to 400 mm. The fundamental deviation is read as the limit nearest zero of the class named in 'from'. f6 over 120 to 180 printed -43/-48 (lower limit inconsistent with f5/f7; the upper, fundamental, value -43 is unaffected).

OSG_JIS.title: Deviation of shafts to be used in commonly used fits (JIS B 0401 extract)
OSG_JIS.note: JIS B 0401 is the Japanese adoption of ISO 286. Prints limit deviations up to 250 mm; fundamental deviation read as the limit nearest zero.

WIKI_BSP.title: British Standard Pipe (size table)
WIKI_BSP.note: Names ISO 7-1:1994 and ISO 228-1:2000. Prints TPI, pitch, major and minor diameter (in and mm), gauge length and tapping drills.

ETB_BSP.title: ISO 228 - Pipe threads where pressure tight joints are not made on the threads
ETB_BSP.note: Major diameter printed to 0.01 mm, G 1/8 to G 4. Its "minor (nut) diameter" column is not the basic minor diameter (it is larger), so it is not compared.

WIKI_NPT.title: National pipe thread (NPT dimensions table)
WIKI_NPT.note: Names ASME B1.20.1 without a year. The 4 1/2 row is printed without engagement values. 1/16 OD printed .313; E1 is reproduced with 0.3125.

UWASHER_NPT.title: NPT basic dimensions chart (reproduces the ANSI B2.1-1968 table)
UWASHER_NPT.note: Equipment retailer; table credited to ANSI B2.1-1968, the predecessor of ASME B1.20.1. 1/16 OD printed .313. 4 in E1 printed 4.38712 (Wikipedia 4.38713; exact value 4.387125).

WIKI_BSW.title: British Standard Whitworth (BSW size table)
WIKI_BSW.note: Names BS 84:2007. Prints the profile constants 55 deg, depth 0.640327p, radius 0.137329p.

EE_WHIT.title: Whitworth British screw threads size chart, BSW and BSF
EE_WHIT.note: Sizes printed as "11/8" etc. read as 1 1/8. Checked against the BS 84 profile formulas: BSW 1/8 minor printed .0903 (formula .0930) and BSF 7/16 minor printed .3363 (formula .3664) look like digit errors. A BSW row printed "4 3/4" carries the 5 in major diameter and is not used.

BF_BSF.title: British Threads - British Standard Fine (BSF table)
BF_BSF.note: Prints TPI, pitch, core (minor) diameter and tapping drills, 3/16 to 1 in. No standard number cited. Its 7/16 core .3663 agrees with the BS 84 profile, so the Engineers Edge .3363 is a digit error.

WIKI_BA.title: British Association screw threads (size table)
WIKI_BA.note: Names BS 93:2008. States pitch = 0.9^n mm, major diameter = 6 p^1.2 mm, both rounded to two significant figures, angle 47.5 deg, depth 0.6p, radius 0.18083p. Table printed for 0 to 10 BA and 25 BA only.

BF_BA.title: British Threads - BA (table, inch)
BF_BA.note: Prints diameters and pitch in inch, 0 to 16 BA. Its inch diameters differ slightly from the metric values converted (0 BA .2360 in against 6.0 mm = .2362 in), so only TPI is compared; diameters come from the BS 93 formula.

WIKI_MT.title: Machine taper (Morse, Jacobs, R8 and HSK tables)
WIKI_MT.note: Morse table: taper ratio, gauge diameter A (mm and in), half angle. Names ISO 296:1991, DIN 228-1, ISO 7388-1/-2, ASME B5.50, ISO 12164 and JIS B 6339 without current editions. R8 given in prose only.

LMS.title: Dimensions of standard tapers (Morse, Jacobs, Brown & Sharpe, Jarno)
LMS.note: Inch. Morse: large end, small end, length, taper per foot, taper per inch, angle from centre. Morse 4 1/2 printed with large end 1.5000 and taper per foot 0.6240; Wikipedia prints 1.4895 in and 1:19.128 (0.6274 per foot).

TNG.title: Taper specifications (NMTB, CAT/V-flange, ISO 7388-1/DIN 69871, BT)
TNG.note: Tables credited to Kennametal catalogue 7060 and to ANSI B5.50, ISO 7388-1, DIN 69871, JIS B 6339 and JMTBA AS-403. CAT and BT in inch with mm in brackets (inch used here); CAT 40 flange printed "2.500 (63.05)", where 2.500 in is 63.50 mm, so the mm figure is a digit error. The page warns its dimensions are not for part construction or inspection.

PARLEC.title: Parlec catalogue p. 6, CAT and BT taper specifications
PARLEC.note: Toolholder maker. Values to 2 decimals without units (inch). Threads printed with pitch ("M16 - 2.0", "5/8" - 11"); recorded as M16 and 5/8-11 for comparison.

notes.steep724: All three are 7:24 tapers (3.5 in per foot, included angle 16.594 deg) with the same gauge diameters; they differ in the flange, the drive slots and the retention knob. ISO 7388-1 (forms A/AD/AF, the DIN 69871 "SK" holder) and ISO 7388-2 (form J, the JIS B 6339 / MAS 403 "BT" holder) are metric; CAT (ASME B5.50, ISO 7388-1 form U) uses an inch thread. Retention knobs (pull studs): ISO 7388-3:2016 (forms AD, AF, UD, UF, JD, JF), ASME B5.50 for CAT and JIS B 6339 for BT. Knob profiles and angles differ between machine builders, so check the machine manual before ordering.
notes.morse: Morse tapers are self-holding (about 1:20, roughly 5/8 in per foot; each size has its own ratio). Gauge diameter = diameter at the gauge line (the large end of the socket). Current standard: ISO 296:1991 (self-holding tapers for tool shanks), with DIN 228-1 the matching German standard. Morse 4 1/2 is rare and the two publishers disagree on it. Included angle = 2 atan(taper per foot / 24).
notes.jacobs: Jacobs tapers hold drill chucks on arbors; they are not Morse tapers and the taper per foot differs between sizes (about 0.59 to 0.98 in per foot). Values as published for the Jacobs Chuck series; the drill chuck tapers of DIN 238 (B-series) are a different, metric family and are not listed here. The JT 6 and JT 33 sizes sit between JT 2 and JT 3 in diameter.
notes.hsk: HSK hollow taper shank with flange face contact. Current standard: ISO 12164-1:2023 (shanks of types A, AB, C, CB and EB); DIN 69893-1 is the original German standard. Size = flange diameter d1 in mm (HSK-A 63 has d1 = 63 mm). HSK holders are clamped from inside by the spindle's clamping mechanism, so there is no pull stud. Only one free publisher found so far for the taper diameters; check the holder maker's drawing.
notes.r8: R8 is a collet and toolholder taper used on knee mills (Bridgeport type), held by a 7/16-20 UNF drawbar. No international standard for R8 was found; dimensions are as published, from one source so far.

WALTER.title: Designation key, Walter Turn cutting inserts (en-gb)
WALTER.note: Maker. Shape letters with corner angles, clearance letters, tolerance classes with d/m/s values in mm, thickness and corner codes. Insert type (position 4), edge and hand letters are shown only as drawings and were not read.

MITSUBISHI.title: Toolholder identification system (external turning), product guide
MITSUBISHI.note: Maker. Clamping system, insert shape, clearance, hand and tool length letters, insert size codes by inscribed circle. Holder style angles are drawings only.

KORLOY.title: Turning insert code system (ISO), catalogue pp. B24-B25 (distributed by Cutwel)
KORLOY.note: Maker. Shape angles for C, D, K, R, S, T and size codes; other columns did not extract legibly.

PRAMET.title: Pramet catalogue (inch edition), toolholder designation key p. T179
PRAMET.note: Maker. Clearance letters N, B, C, P; hand R, L; tool length letters K, M, S, Y. Its holder angle legend uses the ANSI lead-angle convention and is not compared.

KENNAMETAL.title: Turning Inserts Master Catalog, catalog numbering system pp. B4-B7
KENNAMETAL.note: Maker (inch edition; tolerances printed in inch, converted here to mm). Used: tolerance classes C, E, G, H; shape letters whose name and angle were legible together (A, B, H, K, L, O, P, R, S, T, W); insert hand R, L, N; edge F = sharp. The rhombic shape rows and the other edge letters did not extract with a clear pairing and are not used.

YG1.title: Indexable insert catalogue YU-IT23, insert ISO code system pp. 6-7 and external holder code system p. 4
YG1.note: Maker (inch edition; thickness and corner radius printed as inch fractions, converted here to mm). Used: clearance letters, tolerance classes C, E, G, H, insert type (clamping hole and chipbreaker columns), thickness and corner codes, holder clamping letters C, M, P, S, holder styles with approach angle (KAPR), holder hand. Its K, M and U tolerance columns did not extract with a clear column order and are not used.

ZCC.title: Turning toolholder catalogue 2022-2023
ZCC.note: Maker. Approach angle Kr printed for each external holder in the product tables; the style letter is the third character of each designation (for example DCLNR: style L, 95 deg). The page has no letter key of its own. CKNNR is printed as 63 deg in one table and 62.5 deg in the overview.

ISCAR.title: Turning catalogue 2022, ISOTURN designation key (catalogue p. 122, HTML view)
ISCAR.note: Maker. The HTML view is scrambled; used only for insert type A (hole, no chipbreaker), where letter and text were together.

DORMER_PRAMET.title: Workpiece material groups (WMG)
DORMER_PRAMET.note: Maker. Colour and material class for each ISO group.

FMCARBIDE.title: ISO material group
FMCARBIDE.note: Tool supplier. Colour and material class for each ISO group.

CTE.title: M. Eastman, "Inserts show their true colors" (1 April 1999)
CTE.note: Trade magazine. Colours for P, M and K only.

SECO.title: The ISO application standardization
SECO.note: Maker. Meaning of the number after the letter (low numbers: finishing, high thermal load; high numbers: roughing, high mechanical load); not a colour source.

CERATIZIT.title: Bar peeling hints and tips: surface quality
CERATIZIT.note: Maker. N grade with Ra, and an Rz value printed beside each grade (cites DIN 4768, now withdrawn).

WERK24.title: N-grades: identify surface roughness better
WERK24.note: Drawing-reading software publisher. N grade with Ra in micrometres and microinches.

ENGINEERSEDGE.title: Surface roughness conversion chart tables
ENGINEERSEDGE.note: Engineering reference site. N grade with Ra.

MECHENG.title: B. Toulas, Surface roughness chart (17 Dec 2018)
MECHENG.note: Engineering site. N grade with Ra and an Rt value; Ra range by process.

AUTODESK.title: Inventor 2020 help: press fit surface quality (Ra by process)
AUTODESK.note: Software maker. Ra values marked as average application for each process; the range here runs from the smallest to the largest value so marked.

OPTIMAS.title: Hardness conversion table (according to ISO 18265)
OPTIMAS.note: Fastener supplier. For carbon, cast and low alloy steels, heat treated or hot formed. Brinell = 0.95 HV; values in brackets are outside the range of the test method.

BOSSARD.title: Technische Information TG.006: Vergleichstabelle Zugfestigkeit, Härte (g-002-de)
BOSSARD.note: Fastener maker. Based on ISO 18265, for unalloyed and low alloy steels and cast steel; considerable deviations for high alloy or cold worked steels; values in brackets are outside the standard test ranges (Brinell above 450 HB only with a carbide ball).

DORIAN.title: Knurling catalogue (technical section)
DORIAN.note: Maker. Teeth = pi D / P (P = 1/TPI); diametral pitch: teeth = D x DP; 30 deg diagonal: teeth = D x DP x cos 30; blank by trial, change by +/- 0.005 in if the knurl double tracks.

HOMMEL_KELLER.title: Zeus knurling catalogue 2021, technical pages 35-46
HOMMEL_KELLER.note: Maker. CP pitch = 25.4 / TPI mm; DP pitch = pi x 25.4 / DP mm; DIN 403 pitches; form knurling enlarges the diameter (empirical table by material and pitch); cut knurling barely changes it.

NORITAKE.title: Technical support: Grain (grain size tables after JIS R6001, JIS R6010, JIS B4130)
NORITAKE.note: Wheel maker. F4-F220: test-sieve stages; the value used here is the stage 3 (control) sieve aperture, which must retain a set share of the grains, not a mean size. F230-F1200: ds-50 (median) diameter by sedimentation, with a tolerance.

HAPSTONE.title: A. Havrylenko, What is the FEPA grit system? (27 May 2026)
HAPSTONE.note: Sharpening-system maker. Approximate particle size for five F grits; says F is used for grinding wheels and stones and P for coated abrasives, and that F400 and P400 are different sizes. Its FEPA/JIS chart is an image and was not read.

TEDPELLA.title: Abrasive grit grading systems (tables courtesy of 3M)
TEDPELLA.note: Lab supplier. Average particle size in um for ANSI and FEPA P grits. These are coated-abrasive gradings.

STEELDATA.title: Grit size table
STEELDATA.note: Mid-points of the size ranges for ANSI/CAMI graded paper (ANSI B74.18-1996, from the CAMI booklet Coated Abrasives, 1996) and FEPA P graded paper (FEPA 43-GB-1984). Coated-abrasive gradings.

UNITED.title: ANSI standard marking system and wheel configurations (6 Aug 2023)
UNITED.note: US wheel maker. ANSI order: abrasive, grit, grade, bond (example A 24 R BF); grit groups; bond letters.

CGW.title: Vitrified and surface grinding wheels catalogue pages 119-125, as hosted by Travers Tool
CGW.note: Wheel maker catalogue. Example 7 x 1/2 x 1 1/4 RA 46H 8V; its own abrasive codes; grit groups; soft, medium and hard grade letters; structure; bond letters.

NAVY.title: Machinery Repairman training manual, Figure 5-4, standard marking system for grinding wheels except diamond (public domain)
NAVY.note: Six stations: abrasive, grain size, grade, structure, bond, maker's record. Grain size groups; grade A (soft) to Z (hard). The bond and structure lists of the figure were not in the text read.

HST.title: L. Petty, Understanding the marking system for abrasive wheels (2016, updated 2023)
HST.note: UK safety training. Cites BS EN 12413 and BS ISO 525. Specification order abrasive, grit, grade, structure, bond (example WA 60 K 7 V); abrasive and bond codes; structure 1 (dense) to 14 (open); speed stripe colours. Commodious (commodious.co.uk, abrasive wheel marking) prints the same lists word for word, so it is not counted as a second source.

grinding.note: Transcribed from the pages listed, 2026-11-10. Values are as printed. Coarse F grits are graded by sieves and fine F grits by sedimentation, so the size printed for a coarse F grit (Noritake: control sieve aperture) is not the same kind of number as a mean particle size; the ANSI and P values here are for coated abrasives. Nearest-size equivalents are approximate.
